properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves along the coast.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast zone.

* WHEN...Until noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous breaking waves can knock people off their
feet and sweep them into the ocean. Driftwood and debris in
powerful surf can injure or even kill people on the beach
observing the ocean. High surf will result in erosion to
beaches, dunes, and bluffs and may cause damage to roads,
trails, and coastal structures.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant log and debris pile-up on the
beaches and jetties from the high surf last weekend will pose
additional threats to those on the beaches and will exacerbate
coastal erosion.
properties.instruction:

surf zone. This includes staying off jetties, piers, and other
coastal structures. Never turn your back on the ocean and keep
children and pets close. Know the tides and forecast conditions.
Follow warning signs and respect barriers.

parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road
closures expected. Dangerous breaking waves can knock people

debris in powerful surf can injure or even kill people on the

beaches, dunes, and bluffs and may cause damage to roads,
trails, and coastal structures.

beaches and jetties from the high surf last weekend will pose

coastal erosion.

coastal structures. Never turn your back on the ocean and keep
children and pets close. Know the tides and forecast conditions.

* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous surf

* WHERE...South Washington Coast.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until noon PST Saturday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level,
during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays,
sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers.
Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other
structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and
jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach
erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher
than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-lying
shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night. In addition,
the Toke Point tidal gage is forecast to reach 11.2 feet during
high tide Friday afternoon, which is high enough to result in
tidal overflow flooding for a few hours around high tide.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal overflow flooding is
expected. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 13 at 3:44AM PST until November 14 at 6:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of
15 to 20 ft expected. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously
large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of
40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash
over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure.

* WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National
Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast and Northern Monterey
Bay.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through this afternoon.
For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM today to 4 AM PST Sunday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight tonight to 6 PM
PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is
specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves
will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent
infrastructure.

surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.
